sourceStates.title: Adopt vLLM 47a8e415bff1 for GPU serving
sourceStates.body:
## Changes

- Pin GPU vLLM to [`marin-vllm-gpu-20261118-47a8e415bff1`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20261118-47a8e415bff1), built from [marin-community/vllm@47a8e415bff1](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/47a8e415bff17b9376f02d9b92edcc67e962eaee): `config/external/vllm/gpu.toml` and the generated pins, as written by `config/update-external.py --promote-gpu-release` from the release manifest.

| Architecture | Wheel SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| aarch64 | `d013b4815e17d0e642ec5965c09f73fc8703f068010240c9e0457d989768db17` |
| x86_64 | `fc2a147c5d068d389f8094ed137b9f731d2fa81cfe143af575a4c3d2ce8a7962` |

## Motivation

The release adds full decode graphs for GrugMoE ShortConv models and a tuned GB200 expert-GEMM configuration ([marin-community/vllm#130](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/130)): on Hero BF16 at TP1/DP16/EP16, single-request latency fell from about 62 to 20 ms per token. Since the current pin (`0ac9dcb157ee`) it also includes the fork's ShortConv output-buffer changes and FP8 loading tests. Configurations still select `PIECEWISE`; this PR only makes `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` available.

## Qualification

- Fork build and wheel tests on H100 and GB200: [run 44206509048](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/44206509048). The first GB200 attempt failed while collecting the result from a job that had succeeded; the rerun passed.
- Snowball cluster parity on H100 with these pins: the Levanter, vLLM PP1 and vLLM PP2 arms of `tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_backend_parity.py` passed (3 passed in 17m42s). The TPU arm was not run, because this PR changes only the GPU wheel.

Part of #11430.

sourceStates.title: [skyrl] Use standard NCCL buffers for policy and reference roles
sourceStates.body:
Megatron policy and reference roles now resolve to an explicit 4-MiB NCCL SIMPLE buffer, and reference forwarding applies in dedicated and colocated layouts. The previous reference default was 256 KiB; an unset policy value delegated sizing to the runtime. The resolved settings override an inherited small-buffer environment. Explicit role tuning remains available. Colocated reference workers retain larger buffers, so their memory budget must account for that.

NCCL 2.30.7 returned incorrect native C and ProcessGroupNCCL reductions with a 256-KiB buffer. A source-library A/B reproduced the failure and corrected it by bounding the NVLSTree chunk to its FIFO slot. Existing-library 4-MiB controls passed the tested 16–512-MiB range; 1-MiB controls failed at 512 MiB. This mitigation keeps the existing library and strict comparator. The eight-GPU A/B does not qualify every topology or message size.

The regression captures resolved role environment mappings at actor allocation with inherited NCCL_BUFFSIZE=262144. Existing immutable run artifacts are unchanged; these defaults apply to future launches.

Part of #11649

sourceStates.title: [rl] Run Mochi and mixed-task Snowball from presets
sourceStates.body:
Run Mochi and mixed-task Snowball through the shared RL launcher. Mochi starts from the model returned by its production SFT preset. The executor reuses completed SFT training and builds its HF export with tokenizer files. The Snowball SFT-to-RL command passes the supervised mixture's export into RL. A following stage can consume the model from a single exporting RL run.

Mixed presets allocate a fixed share of each training batch to each task family. The installed-agent runtime passes Pi the full request window and reply cap. The mixed presets resolve the Daytona target from the submitting environment. The Mochi one-rack preset uses piecewise CUDA graphs.

The mixed training selection recipe combines the existing one-turn quotas with a released agentic task file pinned by SHA-256 and row count. It applies the full EvalLite exclusion and records admission and removal counts for the released source. Harness-graded tasks require explicit grader admission, and the RL plan requires a Harbor trial mapping for each selected harness-graded dataset.

A checkpointing preset can resume from a finished run's latest committed native checkpoint. If the source advances before the coordinator starts, the error gives both step numbers. The native checkpoint export command accepts `--recover-best` for an ended run. A preset can export the latest checkpoint, the best checkpoint, or skip export.

CPU plan prints compose the native SkyRL configuration and check training family counts when quotas apply. Model-declared training placement preserves the eight existing Snowball launch pins. Authored YAML and CLI overrides reject runner-owned placement. The Mochi default plan was checked against the production training cache.

The Mochi one-rack liveness run completed two optimizer updates and saved the step-2 checkpoint on `4453e9745a` using an explicit published initializer. In step 2, 59.75% of loss-bearing tokens used the synchronized weights with piecewise CUDA graphs enabled. Final RL smoke evidence is gathered on the released P83 stack revision. [Mochi liveness run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fusers-ahmad-checkpoints-mochi-rl-train-medium-ccd0098764-in-f77b2799-2026.11.19.1-coordinator-5caf5432)

This draft includes the trainer runtime and SFT preset changes until those drafts merge. [Trainer runtime](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11711) · [SFT presets](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11712)

sourceStates.title: [sft] Declare Snowball and Mochi training presets
sourceStates.body:
Declare supervised fine-tuning presets that export a Hugging Face model with its own tokenizer for reinforcement learning. Run `python -m experiments.post_training.snowball_sft` or `python -m experiments.post_training.mochi_sft` with `--preset <name>` to print the plan. Add `--run` to launch training and export. Levanter exports the final training step. Hero converts the planned permanent checkpoint and writes the pinned tokenizer and stop token IDs beside the weights in `hf/`. Building an SFT preset with a Grug trainer that cannot export a Hugging Face model raises an error that names the required export.

- Multi-node Levanter GPU meshes put cross-node axes first. Preset plans check the mesh against the allocation and check batch divisibility.
- `HFModel` and `PreparedModel` take a typed `model` configuration that carries the Levanter architecture.
- Snowball runs through Levanter, including the five curriculum SFT trials, compute and log the fraction of routed expert assignments dropped across all positions.
- Levanter SFT jobs resolve the GPU training environment on the coordinator before the worker imports JAX.

Snowball's `openthoughts-32k-4node` puts one conversation in each training example and keeps its first 32,768 tokens. Of 94,334 conversations, 1,815 exceed the context window, including a 32,950-token input observed in the first four-node smoke. The four-node H100 run at Marin revision `20ed09e08e` completed five updates and wrote checkpoint `step-4` and its Hugging Face export. A separate read-only CPU job confirmed the presence of all 79 weight shards named in the index. [First smoke](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-sft-h100-smoke) · [Training job](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-sft-h100-stack-sync) · [Artifact read](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-sft-h100-storage-final)

```text
SNOWBALL_H100_FOUR_NODE_SFT_PASS completed_updates=5 checkpoint=s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/atqamar/claude-one-loop/sft-h100/checkpoints/snowball-h100-four-node-smoke-stack-sync/2026.11.19.1/checkpoints/step-4 export=s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/atqamar/claude-one-loop/sft-h100/checkpoints/snowball-h100-four-node-smoke-stack-sync/2026.11.19.1/hf/step-4
```

Snowball's `mixture-262k-32node` uses the three mixture files from #11120 at revision `c6676c91ef`. It trains for 204 updates at a global batch size of 256, supervises assistant tokens inside each packed document, and exports FP32 weights. A CPU test verified the device ordering and axis groups for the 32-node mesh. The preset awaits an accelerator run. A forced-overflow case reported a drop fraction of 0.5 and matched the unreduced training loss. The existing SFT step names, versions and fingerprints match for both Delphi recipes, Iceball, June Grug, the original Snowball recipe, and the five curriculum trials.

Mochi's `mixture-262k-176node` uses the training configuration of `hero-sft-fullab-step393k-v2` and selects permanent step 400407 for export. On CPU, SkyRL staged a tiny checkpoint export as schema 3 BF16 with split experts, verified its vocabulary with the trainer's check, and read back the fixture's stop token IDs.

The CPU export of the sealed production checkpoint wrote 193 BF16 shards and the pinned tokenizer, with stop token IDs `128001`, `128008`, and `128009`. Its job wrote the artifact before a readback command failed. A separate CPU job verified the artifact and registered the versioned model handle. [Production export](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-mochi-export-step-400407-peer) · [Readback and registration](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fclaude-one-loop-mochi-export-readback)

newFindings.title: [post-training] Mochi hero SFT (step 400,407) weakness analysis: benchmark gaps, trace failures, and candidate target skills
newFindings.body:
## TL;DR

- **Model audited:** Mochi hero SFT step 400,407 (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/exports/mochi-sft/hero-sft-fullab-step393k-v2/step-400407/2af3f828aa-cpu-a1/`). Read-only analysis of the retained Mochi EvalDash snapshot (**12 full-size completed EvalDash benchmark runs**, one per benchmark, out of 46 total recorded runs: 23 `succeeded`, 20 `step_failed`, 2 `infra_failed`, 1 `running`), separate **BFCL x5** runs ([issue 11538](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11538), `k=5`), a separate **SWE-smith 128x8 r6** screen (469 retained / 463 scored attempts), and two other teams' evaluations ([issue 11418](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11418) and [issue 11181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11181)).
- **Comparison against Snowball 10/05 and peer open-weight models (descriptive, configuration-dependent):** Mochi is above the selected Snowball 10/05 observed range on **nine** of the twelve EvalDash benchmarks (`boolq`, `piqa`, `triviaqa`, `truthfulqa`, `humanevalplus`, `mbppplus`, `gsm8k-0shot`, `ifbench`, `mrcr-65k`), inside it on **two** (`ds-1000-local`, `financebench`), and below it on **one** (`winogrande`). The separate BFCL x5 and paired scored SWE-smith readouts also favor Mochi descriptively. Against stronger open-weight reference rows (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, Nemotron-3.5-30B/120B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash), the three clearest weaknesses backed by trace inspection are:
  1. **Long-context multi-needle ordinal retrieval (`mrcr-65k`: 26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08% [89.88–93.12], k=5; Nemotron-3.5-30B 45.75% [44.84–46.91], k=4)** — among 620 prefix-matching items with `score <= 0.9`, 423 matched another same-topic occurrence by a 60-character substring heuristic (331 later than requested, 92 earlier; 323 under literal stripped-output equality: 275 later, 48 earlier).
  2. **Strict verifiable instruction following (`ifbench`: 26.00% strict / 32.33% loose prompt vs Gemma-4 43.44% [42.00–45.00], k=3; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 40.00%, k=1; Nemotron-3.5-120B 38.00%, k=1; Qwen3.6 34.57% [32.33–38.67], k=7)** — lowest strict category means are `repeat` (0.00%), `sentence` (3.57%), `words` (11.76%), and `ratio` (15.91%). Separately, on `gsm8k-0shot` (83.55%), 145/217 misses contain the normalized gold number in the final 250 characters under our regex heuristic, flagging candidates for extractor sensitivity (see Section 2.5).
  3. **Tool-contract sub-weaknesses (BFCL x5 and SWE-smith r6)** — headline BFCL x5 (`73.17%` final-selected record score under the retry rule) sits inside Qwen3.6's observed range (`70.73–75.61%`; mean `73.50%`), but `simple-java` (53.3%), `parallel` (62.9%), and `live-irrelevance` (65.5%) lag; on SWE-smith r6, 69/469 attempts included at least one parsed `read` call with an extra `"command"` key (391/1,707 parsed `read` calls), first named malformed-tool categories in readout-BAD rows were `read` for 12/19, `edit` for 6/19, and `bash` for 1/19, raw `<tool_call>` text appeared in 21/58 exception-free `reward=0` attempts (15 `read`, 6 `edit`), and 289/469 attempts hit `AgentTimeoutError` at 900 s.
- **Major snapshot gaps remain:** In this snapshot, Mochi has no completed full-size score on hard math/reasoning (`aime24`, `math500` full, `olympiadbench`, `gpqa-diamond`), broad knowledge/code-execution (`mmlu-pro`, `cruxeval`, `nupa`), `mrcr` (128K), major agentic suites (`swebench-verified`, `tb2-recovery`, `ot-tblite-recovery`, `bixbench-pi`, `tau3-pi`), or Micro210.

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535).

---

## 1. Benchmark Scorecard (Mochi step 400,407 vs Comparators)

**Comparability, serving, and cohort notes (all cross-model comparisons are descriptive and configuration-dependent):**
- The 12 EvalDash rows for Mochi are single completed full-size runs (`k=1` each) served on H100s (`pp=3, dp=8`, `max_model_len=65536`, `marin-tokenizer-tools` revision `3f6879a`, `tool_call_parser=hermes`, `reasoning_parser=null`, `chat_template_kwargs={}`, PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, generation config from Snowball RLVR Step 92). Note that `reasoning_parser=null` means no reasoning parser was configured on the serve; it does not by itself establish whether thinking was disabled at generation time.
- Snowball 10/05 (`open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) also had `reasoning_parser=null` and `tool_call_parser=hermes` in the checked EvalDash runs, whereas Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`qwen3`), Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (`gemma4`), and Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B (`nemotron_v3`) had native reasoning parsers configured.
- Comparator ranges are **observed ranges** `[min–max]` across retained runs in each cohort, showing cohort count `k` and scored count `n`. The audit retains `succeeded` runs with a populated headline and no recorded policy violations. It applies an 80% coverage floor when both scored and benchmark counts are positive, plus per-benchmark scored-count floors when a positive scored count is reported (`>= 100` for `ds-1000-local`/`bfclparity-pi`, `>= 200` for `ifbench`, `>= 500` for `mrcr-65k`, `>= 1000` for `gsm8k-0shot`); coverage filtering does not prove every comparator run was uncapped.

### 2.1 `mrcr-65k` (26.49%, n=901; all 901 classified, 15 read directly)

Mochi prepends the exact requested 10-character random string on **806/901 (89.46%)** of prompts, and **186/901 (20.6%)** score `> 0.9` on MRCR's graded string-similarity metric. Mean `mrcr_accuracy` declines with needle count and across the four length buckets below 40k (`n_chars // 4`); the single 40k+ item scored 80.78%:

| Slice | n | Mean `mrcr_accuracy` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 needles | 299 | 36.29% |
| 4 needles | 302 | 28.71% |
| 8 needles | 300 | **14.47%** (graded string similarity) |
| 0–10k (`n_chars // 4`) | 325 | 31.68% |
| 10–20k (`n_chars // 4`) | 283 | 27.15% |
| 20–30k (`n_chars // 4`) | 159 | 20.05% |
| 30–40k (`n_chars // 4`) | 133 | 19.66% |
| 40k+ (`n_chars // 4`) | 1 | 80.78% |

Across the **620** items that hit the exact random prefix with `score <= 0.9`:
- **423 / 620 (68.2%)** matched another same-topic occurrence by a 60-character substring heuristic, with **331** matched occurrences later than the requested one and **92** earlier (measured direction; not opportunity-normalized). Under literal stripped-output equality with the same topic heuristic, **323 / 620 (52.1%)** matched another same-topic occurrence (**275** later, **48** earlier).
- **26 / 620 (4.2%)** matched a different-topic assistant turn under the 60-character substring heuristic.
- **171 / 620 (27.6%)** had no classified alternative-turn match under this heuristic (this residual count does not separate paraphrases from partial or truncated outputs).
- The remaining **95 / 901 (10.5%)** failed the exact-prefix check (`score = 0`).

## 3. Proposed Candidate Target Skills (with Fast-Eval Proposals and Non-Eval Data Ideas)

*Data hygiene rule:* **Eval-side traces and benchmark prompts/outputs are never used as training data.** Every training data proposal below relies exclusively on freshly synthesized or non-eval open templates verified programmatically. Probe runtimes below are rough estimates and not yet measured on Mochi's serve.

### Proposal 1: Long-Context Ordinal Multi-Needle Retrieval and Verbatim Copy
- **Target gap:** Largest observed deficit vs peers (`mrcr-65k` 26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08% and Nemotron-3.5-30B 45.75%), with 423/620 prefix-matching low-score items matching a different same-topic occurrence by 60-character substring (323 under literal stripped-output equality), predominantly later than requested.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 100–200 item synthetic multi-needle probe at 8K–64K context (2/4/8 repeated-topic needles, querying the *k*-th 1-indexed occurrence with a random prefix), scored deterministically in Python by exact prefix and string similarity without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically synthesize multi-turn dialogues (8K–64K tokens) mixing filler turns with 2–12 repeated requests on fresh non-MRCR topics, paired with final-turn ordinal retrieval queries distributed uniformly over *k* from 1 to *N* (covering both `/think` counting chains and `/nothink` direct-copy targets).

### Proposal 2: Strict Verifiable Constraint Following and Output Discipline
- **Target gap:** Strict instruction-following gap vs peers (`ifbench` 26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 40.00%, Nemotron-3.5-120B 38.00%, Qwen3.6 34.57%), with `repeat` (0.00%), `sentence` (3.57%), `words` (11.76%), and `ratio` (15.91%) lowest.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 200-item held-out synthetic constraint suite covering word/sentence/ratio/repeat/format/no-preamble constraints, scored purely by deterministic Python verifiers without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically compose fresh prompts combining 1–3 verifiable lexical/structural constraints (forbidden/required words, exact sentence/word counts, keyword-per-sentence, ratio bounds, strict JSON/markdown structure, no preamble/postscript), generate candidates, and **rejection-sample strictly using deterministic Python verifiers** (keeping only 100%-passing responses across both `/think` and `/nothink` formats).

### Proposal 3: Tool-Schema Adherence and Abstention Across Diverse Tool Contracts
- **Target gap:** Addresses the concrete tool-contract weaknesses observed in BFCL x5 (`simple-java` 53.3%, `parallel` 62.9%, `live-irrelevance` 65.5%) and the extra-`"command"` `read`/malformed-call defects observed in SWE-smith r6 (69/469 attempts with extra `"command"` on parsed `read`; 12/19 readout-`BAD` first-tool `read`; 21/58 exception-free `reward=0` raw `<tool_call>` text).
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 150–200 item single-turn synthetic tool-calling probe testing: (a) unfamiliar file/code tool schemas deliberately distinct from `str_replace_editor` (checking valid Hermes JSON and zero undeclared keys), (b) irrelevance/abstention prompts requiring an explicit empty tool list or required artifact, and (c) parallel and typed-argument multi-call prompts. Graded deterministically by JSON-schema and AST checks without container spinup.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Synthesize diverse tool definitions (varying parameter names across file readers/editors, SQL/API clients, and typed Java/JS/Python signatures) with programmatically verified trajectories teaching strict adherence to declared JSON schemas, calibrated abstention when no tool applies or required arguments are missing, and parallel call arrays.

newFindings.title: [post-training] Offline Mochi top-K logit distillation for Snowball SFT
newFindings.body:
Adds offline top-K logit distillation to Snowball SFT and the scripts for a one-hour ablation that trains Snowball on stored Mochi (SFT step 400407) top-20 soft targets.

- **Loss:** `next_token_loss` takes optional teacher top-K ids and log-probs. The soft term is cross-entropy to the teacher distribution renormalized over its top K, on assistant tokens only. It is added to the hard loss as `hard + alpha * soft`, so the hard term keeps weight 1. `trainer.distill_alpha` defaults to 0, and at 0 the loss equals the existing loss exactly (`test_distillation.py`).
- **Data:** `teacher_topk` and `teacher_validation_cache` on the E12 data config carry `teacher_ids` / `teacher_logprobs` through packing. Eval reports `eval/teacher_nll/loss` and `eval/teacher_kl/loss` on the held-out teacher slice.
- **Scripts** (`experiments/post_training/teacher_distill/`):
  - `prep_slice.py` packs a seeded slice of the SFT mixture into 262,144-token rows (480 train, 32 held-out).
  - `assemble.py` joins the rows with the teacher scores into a cache.
  - `launch_arms.py` submits arm A (hard only, alpha 0) and arm B (alpha 0.5) from the existing one-hour FP32 template. Both arms use the same data order, steps and LR.
- **Scorer:** the vLLM prompt-logprob scorer is on branch `task/504-score`. It is not part of this PR, because it builds on the Mochi serve config from the BFCL branch.

## Result (one seed, 60 steps)

| Step 59 | A: hard only | B: hard + 0.5 soft | B − A |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Held-out NLL | 0.54430 | 0.54432 | +0.00002 |
| KL to Mochi top-20 | 0.07584 | 0.07525 | −0.00059 |
| `eval/loss` | 0.49500 | 0.49500 | 0.00000 |
| `eval/e12/loss` | 0.02941 | 0.02954 | +0.00013 |

- **NLL:** no difference in held-out NLL.
- **KL:** B moves 0.8% closer to Mochi, and the gap grows at every eval.
- **Limits:** 60 steps at LR 2e-5 barely move the model, and there are no downstream evals.
- **Speed:** both arms run about 2.7 times slower than the template. This looks like a fixed per-step cost from carrying the teacher arrays; the hard arm also loads them. It has not been profiled.

W&B runs: `marin-long-loop/task504-distill-{a-hard,b-soft}-20261119r2`.

qualification.body:
🤖 The three-rack Snowball integration smoke passed with `NCCL_BUFFSIZE=4194304` for trainer and inference workers and the launch gate. Snowball is the 67B model with approximately 2B active parameters used to test the long-loop pipeline for Mochi. The run used 64 trainer GPUs (PP2/CP4/EP4/DP8) and two 64-GPU inference engines on 192 GB200s, from frozen workspace source `47e13d52b6c429b181233dd56fddf78d621b8144`.

Both optimizer updates applied with zero skipped steps. The original strict check compared replicated trainer parameter bytes across data-parallel peers and replayed weight transfers to every inference receiver. It requires zero mismatches and complete receiver byte coverage. Checks completed for the initial weights and after each update; the #11650 comparator-chunking workaround was off. All 192 GPUs passed the launch gate's Torch collectives and vLLM PyNccl communicator initialization. The library remained unpatched NCCL 2.30.7. The [isolated library A/B](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11649#issuecomment-6977654297) remains the mechanism test; this run qualifies the 4 MiB configuration in the full integration topology.

Final native checkpoint 2 passed structural readback: 74,572 indexed extents fit 64 rank files totaling 539,416,455,106 bytes. A full tensor restore was not run. All 48 GPU tasks succeeded and released, with no failures or preemptions. Controller task durations account for 98.33356 GB200-hours; this is not provider billing.

Policy-train times were 68.960 and 45.301 seconds. Update-loop durations, from entry through checkpoint completion, were 898.232 and 350.888 seconds. Evaluation was disabled. Native placement and phase records cover all 64 trainers and 128 inference GPUs; actual graph capture was confirmed in both inference engine leaders. Update-2 GPU-busy sampling covers only 48/64 trainers and 100/128 inference GPUs. Two Snowball updates do not establish steady-state or 535B Mochi performance.

[Certification and evidence](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-long-loop%2Fevidence%2Fsnowball67-certification%2Fcertification.json) (Marina login): `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-long-loop/evidence/snowball67-certification/certification.json`, SHA-256 `9018a903b2d9eed6883c4071efa5698303c0eec426fa5f52fdbcbcab2bb86de2`. The certification and nine selected summary JSON files were read back byte-for-byte; `publication.json` lists those files. #11656 sets the role buffers to 4 MiB to avoid the small-buffer corruption; this run supplies its integration qualification.
